previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease, status post subtotal colectomy, was admitted for recurrent left lower quadrant abdominal pain and increased loose stools. He had self-increased his azathioprine (Imuran) dose prior to admission. Initial management included IV methylprednisolone for a presumed Crohn’s flare and IV Imuran, but the latter was discontinued due to developing thrombocytopenia. Imaging, including MRI abdomen, showed stable inflammatory changes in the sigmoid colon without abscess or stricture. Pain initially localized to the left lower quadrant later radiated to the right lower quadrant and right testicle, prompting evaluation for nephrolithiasis, which was ruled out by renal ultrasound and KUB. He was transitioned from IV to oral pain medications and restarted on ciprofloxacin after a brief trial of rifaximin. His platelet count normalized after stopping Imuran, and he was discharged home on oral prednisone, ciprofloxacin, and pantoprazole, with plans to initiate a new immunomodulatory agent through outpatient gastroenterology follow-up. Opioid medications were not prescribed at discharge due to a history of misuse.
